title: Chemical symbols
competency: Identify and write chemical symbols of common elements.

keywords.def: A shorthand way of writing an element, like O for oxygen.

en.text: A chemical symbol is a shorthand way of writing an element. A one-letter symbol is a capital, like O. A two-letter symbol has a capital then a small letter, like Ca. Some symbols come from Latin names: Na is sodium from Natrium, K is potassium from Kalium.

screens.title: Two Cs
screens.ask: Carbon and calcium both start with C. Can they both use the symbol C?
opts: No, each element needs its own symbol
screens.after:
No. Each element needs its own symbol, or symbols would mix up.
Carbon is C. Calcium gets two letters: Ca.
screens.best: No, each element needs its own symbol

screens.title: 3.1.2 Chemical symbols
paras: Scientists use symbols as short names for elements.
An atomic symbol is a shorthand way of representing elements or atoms of an element.
Every element has its own symbol. No two elements can have the same symbol.

screens.title: How to write symbols of elements
paras: A symbol comes from the first letter, or the first letter plus another letter, of the element's name.
The name may be the common name or the Latin/Greek name.
A one-letter symbol is a capital. With two letters, the first is capital and the second is small.
screens.note: S is sulfur, O is oxygen, K is potassium (from the Latin Kalium).

screens.title: Why not always the first letter?
paras: Carbon and calcium both begin with "C".
Carbon gets C. Calcium gets two letters: Ca.
In the same way hydrogen is H and helium is He.

screens.title: Writing the symbol of calcium
steps: Start with the first letter of the name: C.
Is C already used? Yes, carbon is C.
Add another letter from the name: a.
Write the first letter capital, the second small.

Key words
defs: A shorthand way of writing an element, like O for oxygen.

screens.text: Choose the correct chemical symbol for silicon.
screens.why:
Silicon starts with S, but S alone is sulfur.
So silicon takes a second letter: i.
The first letter is capital, the second is small.
Answer: Si.
"SI" is wrong: the second letter must be small.
screens.clue: The second letter is always small.

screens.title: Match symbol and element
screens.why:
These symbols come from Latin names (Table 3.2).
Na is from Natrium = sodium. K is from Kalium = potassium.
Fe is from Ferrum = iron. Cu is from Cuprum = copper.
Ag is from Argentum = silver.
screens.clue: Think of the Latin names: Natrium, Kalium, Ferrum, Cuprum, Argentum.
screens.text: Match each symbol to its element. These symbols come from Latin names.
Which symbol for chlorine is written correctly?
screens.why:
Chlorine has a two-letter symbol: C and l.
The first letter is always a capital: C.
The second letter is always small: l.
Answer: Cl.
CL, cl and cL break the capital-then-small rule.

screens.ask: Write the chemical symbol of calcium: ___
screens.why:
Calcium starts with C.
But carbon already uses C.
So calcium adds its second letter, a, written small.
Answer: Ca.
screens.clue: Two letters: C and a small letter.

screens.text: Spot the mistake. Ayele says the symbol of copper is Co, because copper starts with "Co". What is wrong?
opts: Copper is Cu, from the Latin Cuprum
screens.ans: Copper is Cu, from the Latin Cuprum
screens.why:
Copper's symbol does not come from its English name.
It comes from the Latin name Cuprum.
Capital C, small u: Cu.
So Ayele is wrong: copper is Cu.
Co is the symbol of a different element, cobalt.

items.text: True or false: Ca is the symbol of sodium.
items.why:
Ca is the symbol of calcium (Table 3.1).
Sodium comes from the Latin Natrium.
So sodium is Na.
The statement is false.

items.text: True or false: water is not an element.
items.why:
An element cannot be broken into simpler substances.
Water can be split into hydrogen and oxygen.
So water is a compound, not an element.
The statement is true.

items.text: True or false: elements are pure substances.
items.why:
An element has only one kind of atom.
Nothing else is mixed in.
So an element is a pure substance.
The statement is true.

items.text: Choose the correct chemical symbol for silicon.
items.why:
Silicon starts with S, but S alone is sulfur.
So silicon takes a second letter: i.
The first letter is capital, the second is small.
Answer: Si.
"SI" is wrong: the second letter must be small.

items.text: Which element does the symbol "C" stand for?
items.why:
A one-letter symbol is the first letter of the name.
Carbon got the single letter C.
Calcium is Ca, chlorine is Cl, copper is Cu (Cuprum).
Answer: carbon.
items.clue: Which one got the single letter?

items.why:
Potassium → K, from the Latin Kalium.
Iodine → I. Boron → B.
Helium → He, because H is hydrogen.
Chlorine → Cl, because C is carbon.
Gold → Au, from the Latin Aurum.
items.clue: Some symbols come from Latin names.
items.text: Match each element to its chemical symbol.

items.why:
Calcium → Ca, because C is carbon.
Copper → Cu, from the Latin Cuprum.
Hydrogen → H. Lithium → Li.
Silver → Ag, from the Latin Argentum.

test.text: What is the chemical symbol of oxygen?
test.why:
Oxygen has a one-letter symbol: its first letter.
A one-letter symbol is always a capital.
So oxygen is O, not o or Ox.
Answer: O.

test.text: Which element has the symbol Fe?
test.why:
Fe does not match an English name.
It comes from the Latin Ferrum.
Ferrum means iron.
Answer: iron. (Fluorine is F, lead is Pb, phosphorus is P.)

test.text: True or false: a two-letter symbol is written with both letters in capitals.
test.why:
In a two-letter symbol, the first letter is capital.
The second letter is small.
Example: Mg, not MG.
The statement is false.

test.text: The Latin name of lead is Plumbum. What is the chemical symbol of lead?
test.why:
Lead's symbol comes from its Latin name, Plumbum.
Take P, then another letter of the name: b.
Capital first, small second: Pb.
Answer: Pb.

test.text: Why can helium not use the symbol H?
test.why:
No two elements can share a symbol.
Hydrogen already uses H.
So helium adds a second letter: He.
Answer: H is hydrogen.
